playbook:
When I hold K and I'm first to act or the opponent checks to me, I bet for value and to apply pressure.

When I hold Q and I'm first to act, I default to checking for pot control in neutral-stack situations; I switch to a bet when I'm behind in chips or the opponent is short-stacked (i.e., stealing becomes profitable).

When I hold Q and the opponent bets a single chip after I checked, I call — Q has enough showdown equity to contest small bets unless stack dynamics or prior actions indicate my hand is almost certainly dominated.

When I hold J and I'm first to act in a neutral- or small-stack situation, I check to control the pot and avoid low-equity bluffs.

When I hold J and I'm behind in chips but not catastrophically short, I will occasionally open with a bet to apply pressure and attempt a steal; use this selectively (more likely when I need to claw back chips).

When the opponent checks to me and I have a marginal hand (J or Q), I bet to try to steal only when my stack position or opponent tendencies make aggression likely profitable; otherwise check for pot control.

When the opponent bets after my check and I hold J or Q and the bet is a single chip, I call for showdown equity; fold only to larger bets or strong information showing a K.

When facing small one-chip bets with J or Q I prioritize calling for showdown equity; with larger bets or repeated aggression I fold marginal hands more readily.

When I open with a bet, prefer it as a value/pressure action with K and as a selective steal with Q or J depending on stack dynamics.

Adjust aggression as stacks shift: more stealing (bet as opener) when I am behind or opponent is short; more pot control (check) when stacks are neutral or opponent is ahead.

Always declare my actual card honestly at showdown; never misdeclare.
